data.name: Saraiyah
data.gender_notes: Saraiyah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: My God has made a joke
data.long_meaning: Saraiyah is a Hebrew name derived from the biblical figure Sarah, meaning 'lady, noblewoman, princess'. The name is believed to have originated from the Hebrew word sarah, meaning 'my God has made a joke'. This name was borne by the matriarch Sarah in the Old Testament, who was promised a child in her old age through the intervention of God. Sarah's laughter at God's promise led to the name 'Saraiyah'. In the New Testament, Sarah is also mentioned as the wife of Abraham and the mother of Isaac.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reminder of God's sense of humor and his ability to bring laughter and joy into our lives.
data.etymology: Saraiyah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My God has made a joke.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saraiyah total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: שריה
in_hebrew.meaning: היא ששרה, אדוני ה' הוא המושיע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שריה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'היא ששרה' או 'אדוני ה' הוא המושיע'. השם נגזר משורש 'שרה' שפירושו 'שרה' או 'זמר', ו'-יה' הוא סיומת שמשמעותה 'ה' הוא'. השם שריה מופיע בתנ'ך כצורה שונה של השם שרה, ומשמעותו היא 'אדוני ה' הוא המושיע' או 'היא ששרה לה'.

in_greek.name: Σαραΐα
in_greek.meaning: Αυτή που τραγουδά, Κύριος ο Θεός είναι ο Σωτήρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σαραΐα είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος שריה, που σημαίνει 'Αυτή που τραγουδά' ή 'Κύριος ο Θεός είναι ο Σωτήρ'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα, αλλά η εβραϊκή ρίζα του ονόματος σχετίζεται με τη λέξη 'שרה' που σημαίνει 'τραγουδά' ή 'ζεί'.

in_english.name: Saraiyah
in_english.meaning: She who sings, princess, or Lord God is the Savior
in_english.long_meaning: The name Saraiyah originates from the Hebrew name שריה (Sarayah), which means 'she who sings' or 'princess'. It is related to the name Sarah and carries the connotation 'Lord God is the Savior'. In Christian tradition, Saraiyah symbolizes a person who brings joy and praise through song, reflecting a deep spiritual connection with God. Historically, the name has been used across various Christian cultures, signifying a heritage of faith and worship.

data.cultural_impact: The name Saraiyah carries a rich cultural significance as it is derived from the biblical figure Sarah, who is a prominent character in Jewish and Christian traditions. Her story of faith and laughter in the face of God's promises has been a source of inspiration and intrigue for generations. The name Saraiyah is also a reminder of the importance of faith, trust, and patience in the face of life's challenges.
data.spiritual_significance: Saraiyah is a name steeped in spiritual significance, as it is derived from the Old Testament matriarch Sarah, who is revered as a symbol of faith and trust in God's promises. The name represents the notion that God can make the impossible possible, even in the midst of one's old age or seemingly insurmountable challenges. Saraiyah also embodies the idea of laughter and joy in the face of adversity, illustrating the importance of maintaining a positive outlook and a sense of humor in one's spiritual journey. Ultimately, the name Saraiyah serves as a reminder of the power and promise of God, and the importance of maintaining faith and hope in the face of life's uncertainties.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Saraiyah means "my princess" in Hebrew, symbolizing the deep reverence and devotion Christians hold for God-given womanhood and the inner royalty of every believer. In faith, every woman is a precious princess in God's sight, worthy of love, respect, and protection.

biblical_reference.note: In the Bible, Saraiyah refers to a Levite who was a leader of the people during the time of Nehemiah.

historical_references.reference: In Exodus 3:1, God speaks to Moses from the burning bush, identifying himself as 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'. This passage indicates that these patriarchs were revered as gods within the Hebrew religious tradition centuries before the emergence of Christianity.

In the New Testament book of Acts (7:2-4), Stephen describes Sarai (later named Sarah) as 'the woman who conceived offspring from Abraham after he was past the age of masculinity, who herself bore a son Isaac'. This passage indicates that Sarai was a significant figure in the early Christian understanding of the patriarchs' lives.
